findings.title: Translation path never loads fallback locale files
findings.body: I18n.translate still only calls load_locale for config.locale, and the new ensure_loaded! helper is invoked only from ApplicationController#set_locale. The accelerator otherwise refuses to load YAML except for that one locale, while I18n::Backend::Fallbacks looks up SiteSetting.default_locale and :en in memory. Jobs, mailers, I18n.with_locale, and any I18n.t outside that before_filter therefore miss fallback strings (and plural rules) that exist on disk. Calls with no interpolation args then freeze the "translation missing" result in the LRU cache, so later loading the fallback locale does not repair that key until restart or eviction.

findings.title: Cached translations ignore the fallback locale
findings.body: The no-argument translation cache key is only the key, I18n.locale, and backend object id. FallbackLocaleList now resolves missing keys through SiteSetting.default_locale, which admins can change at runtime without I18n.reload!. A string that was filled from the old site locale stays cached under the user locale, so after a default-locale change users of incomplete locales keep seeing the previous language for hot keys until process restart or LRU eviction.

findings.title: Fallbacks turned on in development and test
findings.body: config.i18n.fallbacks = true was previously limited to production, profile, and the cloud66 production file, so development and test left missing keys visible. This initializer always includes I18n::Backend::Fallbacks and installs FallbackLocaleList, with no environment guard. In development and test, a key missing from the current locale now silently becomes the site-locale or English string instead of the missing-translation marker, which hides incomplete locale files and can change specs that set a non-English locale and assert on missing keys or exact untranslated output.
